title: Staged network gating and quiet-rollout lanes for enterprise on‑prem / VPC private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers requesting private/VPC/on‑prem deployments frequently hit two blockers in parallel: (1) strict egress/ingress policies (air‑gapped or limited proxy) and (2) reluctance to take disruptive runtime/component upgrades. Current intake funnels treat these as a single monolithic risk which causes long lead times and inconsistent prioritization.

Proposal: Create a two-axis staging gate and "quiet rollout" lanes that decouple 'network readiness' from 'upgrade permissibility'. The goal is to allow low-risk functional onboarding (prefix/KV cache setup, telemetry-lite, API tokens) via a quiet rollout path while a parallel remediation lane drives the required network upgrades (bastion/proxy templates, signed image delivery, kernel/driver upgrade windows). This reduces time-to-first-success for customers while preserving safety for restrictive environments.

Scope: PM orchestration + runbooks + console onboarding changes + dedicated support playbook + a small set of non-breaking compatibility shims to allow runtime to operate without immediate host upgrades. Excludes forced kernel/driver changes until customer consents and a maintenance window is scheduled.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook and decision matrix published in Confluence: maps customer signals to 'quiet rollout' vs 'remediation lane'
Console checkbox and intake form fields added: 'Allow quiet rollout with limited telemetry' and 'Agree to staged remediation plan'
Pilot onboarding with 3 enterprise customers completed and metrics recorded: time-to-first-success reduced by >=50% compared to baseline
Support playbook created with escalation paths (SRE, Security, Solutions) and templated legal/contract wording for limited telemetry
Two non-breaking compatibility shims delivered by Eng (proxy-adapter v1 and signed-image fetch shim) with PRs merged and smoke tests passing
updates: 2025-02-11 - Kickoff: alignment call with Solutions, SRE, and Security. Agreed to prototype 'quiet rollout' for customers with strict egress but willing to accept telemetry-lite.

2025-02-18 - Decision: do NOT require immediate runtime kernel upgrades for quiet rollout; instead implement compatibility shim + strict telemetry opt-in. Security requested a list of telemetry keys; Solutions to provide mapping.
2025-02-24 - Eng noted impact on autoscaling: quiet rollout instances must use conservative batching and disable aggressive caching until KV cache validation completes. Added ENG-4219 as dependency.
2025-03-01 - Draft runbook created: Confluence draft link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/Quiet+Rollout+Runbook (internal). Please review by 2025-03-07.
2025-03-03 - Pilot customers identified: CS-11832 (finance-software), CS-11910 (healthcare-analytics), CS-11942 (edge-manufacturing). Solutions Engs assigned to each pilot.
2025-03-05 - Security review requested (SR-9901). Security requested data retention TTL for telemetry and approval flow for signed-image fetch. Marked security_review_required = true.
risks: Customers may opt into quiet rollout then decline remediation, causing long-term technical debt in customer fleets
Compatibility shims might mask real issues and delay necessary upgrades, affecting performance or reliability later
Telemetry-lite could be insufficient for diagnosing production incidents, increasing MTTD for pilot customers
Legal/compliance concerns for regulated customers if any telemetry is enabled; requires templated legal language and opt-in audit trail
decision_notes: Chosen approach: two-axis gating (network readiness, upgrade permissibility) with explicit customer consent for quiet rollout. This preserves ability to ship value quickly while retaining a path to full compliance.

Rejected alternatives: (1) 'Hard block' requiring all upgrades before any onboarding — rejected as it increased time-to-first-success and lost PLG momentum; (2) 'Full permissive rollout' with silent upgrades — rejected due to compliance and stability concerns.
Engineering will expose a 'compatibility-mode' flag in the private control plane to opt a tenant into quiet rollout. UX will require explicit checkbox and signed acknowledgement.
